page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused instance configured with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 32 physical Intel cores with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 128 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8) matrix multiplication extensions. The server does not bundle local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent filesystem needs.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong multi-threaded compute capability and high execution efficiency for vectorized workloads. In PassMark, the instance achieved a CPU score of 69,148.07 and recorded a top-tier database operation score of 33,231.61. Geekbench multi-core scoring reached 18,694.0, highlighted by strong code compilation performance with Clang (44,250.0) and top-decile image processing (18,377.0). In web serving benchmarks, throughput achieved a top-tier rate of 90.05 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET throughput reached 71.84 million operations per second. CPU-based LLM inference maintained strong prompt processing rates across small and medium model sizes, processing 2,766.2 tokens per second on 135M models and 228.78 tokens per second on 7B models.

With its high core density and compact memory footprint per thread, n4-highcpu-64 delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound architectures where extra memory allocations would remain idle. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and zero complimentary IPv4 addresses are tradeoffs that require architectural allowances for external storage and networking configuration. The instance fits high-concurrency compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, batch image processing, and distributed database services.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 32 physical Intel cores, paired with 128 GB of RAM and 260 MB of L3 cache. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance incorporates hardware acceleration for AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets, though it excludes local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results show high-throughput processing, achieving 90.05 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and top-tier database operation scores of 33,231.61 in PassMark. Multi-threaded performance is further demonstrated by 71.84 million Redis SET operations per second and strong Geekbench compilation scores. Because memory capacity is capped at 2.0 GB per vCPU, the instance provides cost-efficient execution for CPU-heavy tasks without over-provisioning RAM. It is suited for CI/CD compilation farms, web servers, image processing pipelines, and distributed data services.
